what: Healthcare for the Homeless - Houston provides primary, dental, behavioral and street-based care for people experiencing homelessness.
It reports clinics and outreach across Houston, including dental services.
Its annual report and federal service return use different patient and visit definitions that need reconciliation.
strengths: An established local clinical delivery route addresses unmet care needs.
Original annual reports, federal service data and audited accounts permit an explicit, if partial, cost and activity model.
Finite dental-pain scenarios preserve counterfactual care, possible harm and funding-response uncertainty.
reservations: The annual report and federal data disagree on dental visits; completed symptomatic episodes and causal relief remain unmeasured.
The reported 659 depression screening/follow-up cases are not 659 patients treated for depression, so that pathway receives no modeled credit.
A funded county dental project was terminated for staffing and priority reasons; current gift-created capacity is unverified.

sections.what: HHH provides integrated primary, dental, behavioral health and outreach care. Its 2025 annual report lists 6,433 people and 19,166 visits, while the federal UDS return lists 2,965 patients and 15,986 clinic visits plus 59 virtual visits under different, unreconciled reporting scopes. The UDS identifies 1,499 dental clinic visits and 595 dental patients. This partial model quantifies finite dental-pain relief only; other clinical benefits are unestimated, not assumed absent.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 UDS measure counts 659 patients screened for depression with follow-up documented as appropriate. That measure can include negative screens and does not establish 659 depressed people treated. Its separate remission cohort includes 55 eligible patients, with the outcome numerator suppressed; it is not a substitute denominator. The annual report lists 3,219 dental visits versus 1,499 UDS dental clinic visits, so completed symptomatic episodes and reporting scope require reconciliation. [Federal UDS workbook](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/H80-2025.xlsx) [Annual report](https://www.homeless-healthcare.org/s/FINAL-2025-Impact-Report.pdf)
sections.qualitative: Local integrated care plausibly meets substantial need, but visits do not prove incremental health gains. [Harris County file 26-5142](https://harriscountytx.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=8167289&GUID=9F12FC50-645B-4A78-B668-6049CC4D835E&FullText=1), passed August 17, 2026, terminated a $70,000 dental project that HHH could not implement because of changing priorities and staffing challenges. The [original agreement](https://harriscountytx.legistar.com/View.ashx?M=F&ID=15756863&GUID=E060471F-2059-41E2-8A54-E101BF76C76E) records no reimbursement as of May 31, 2026. This does not mean all dental care ceased; it does show that money alone did not resolve that project’s implementation constraint. The 2024 audit also raises liquidity and staffing-contract concerns.
sections.cost: The model retains the whole organization’s unaudited 2025 expense of $7,844,806, but quantifies only a narrower dental-pain benefit pathway. Using the clearly defined federal UDS series of 1,499 dental clinic visits, the central conditional illustration is $55.6 million per 10 Houston QALYs; the weighted signed scenario mixture is $30.3 million. Neither is a current marginal-donation price. Dental completion, alternative care, symptom relief, utility, duration and cash response are judgment priors rather than measured HHH effects. The depression pathway is unestimated pending a valid treated-patient denominator. [UDS workbook](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/H80-2025.xlsx) [Annual report](https://www.homeless-healthcare.org/s/FINAL-2025-Impact-Report.pdf)
sections.funding: Donor recommendation: HOLD. A city street-medicine agreement described a $700,000 two-year envelope with an initial term ending August 31, 2026; renewal is unverified. The separate $70,000 county dental project was terminated because HHH could not implement it, not because its gift gap was filled. The 2024 audit disclosed a $525,000 credit line due March 17, 2026; renewal and current liabilities are unverified. A current staffed care plan, grant restrictions and a priced incremental giving path are needed before recommending a gift. [City agreement](https://houston.novusagenda.com/agendapublic/CoverSheet.aspx?ItemID=35206&MeetingID=750) [County termination](https://harriscountytx.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=8167289&GUID=9F12FC50-645B-4A78-B668-6049CC4D835E&FullText=1)

model.costScope: Whole 2025 unaudited organizational expense divided by a narrower UDS dental-only benefit pathway. Historical exploratory whole-cost/partial-benefit proxy, not current marginal gift price. Annual report 3219 dental visits versus UDS1499 remains unresolved; UDS selected as the narrower clearly defined series. Cross-pathway overlap multiplier removed because there is only one quantified benefit pathway.
model.geographicAttribution: Care sites and patient ZIP rows support local delivery, but 449 of 2,965 UDS patients are grouped as Other ZIP Codes and some small cells are suppressed. The modeled 95–100% Houston-metro benefit share is a judgment, not measured residence.
model.formula: dentalQalys = dentalVisits / visitsPerEpisode * symptomCompletion * incrementalRelief * dentalUtility * dentalYears; allPopulationQalys = (dentalQalys - harmQalys) * cashResponse; editionQalys = allPopulationQalys * houstonShare; pricePer10 = 10 * costUSD / positive editionQalys
model.counterfactual: Other providers, including Harris Health, may supply some care. Visits count only to the extent they yield additional symptomatic relief versus that alternative; completion and alternative-care shares are unverified judgments.
model.attribution: Whole-recipient expense is retained. Only dental-pain relief is quantified; depression, primary care, behavioral care and outreach benefits remain unestimated. No benefit from the terminated county project is credited.
model.uncertainty: Very low confidence, partial-health model. UDS/annual-report activity scopes are unreconciled. Scenario weights are subjective, not calibrated probabilities; the favorable case drives most weighted positive benefit. Marginal gift impact and staffing response are unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: UDS dental clinic visits divided by assumed visits per symptomatic episode, then assumed completion, incremental relief, finite utility and duration; not observed cured patients.

sensitivity: Weighted signed Houston QALYs = 2.585799921875; whole expense divided by that mixture gives $30338023.965565067 per 10 QALYs.
Removing the favorable world and renormalizing gives $150230102.5852357 per 10 Houston QALYs.
The 3,219 annual-report visits and 1,499 UDS dental clinic visits are not interchangeable. A larger numerator cannot be assumed without reconciling scope.
Harm and null worlds have no positive cost-effectiveness price; their signed QALYs remain in the mixture.
